faqs.answer: 17 g of coffee to 220 g of water at 1:13 is the standard recipe. That is one heaping AeroPress scoop, with water up to the 4 mark on the chamber.
faqs.question: How much coffee do I put in an AeroPress?

faqs.answer: 85 C, about 185 F, is the official recipe. It is cooler than pour-over water, which keeps a fast brew from turning bitter. Light roasts can take up to 96 C.
faqs.question: What temperature water for AeroPress?

faqs.answer: Brew a concentrate and add hot water afterwards. Use 20 g of coffee with 200 g of water in the chamber, press, then add 100 g of hot water to the mug. The chamber only holds about 260 ml.
faqs.question: How do I make a big mug with an AeroPress?

faqs.answer: You flip the AeroPress upside down so no coffee drips through before you press. It uses the same 1:13 ratio and a 90-second steep. It gives a fuller cup, but flipping a brewer full of hot coffee needs care.
faqs.question: What is the inverted AeroPress method?

faqs.answer: Usually the water was too hot or the steep ran too long. Drop to 85 C, keep the steep to 90 seconds, and press gently. A finer grind can also over-extract, so stay at medium-fine.
faqs.question: Why is my AeroPress coffee bitter?

felicityNote: The AeroPress is the one I take on trips. One scoop, water to the 4 mark, two minutes, and it tastes like home.

howToSteps.name: Set up the AeroPress
howToSteps.text: Put a paper filter in the cap, rinse it with hot water, and set the chamber on your mug. Add 17 g of medium-fine coffee.

howToSteps.name: Pour and stir
howToSteps.text: Pour 220 g of water at about 85 C over the grounds. Stir gently three times, then put the plunger in just far enough to seal the chamber.

howToSteps.name: Wait 90 seconds
howToSteps.text: Let the coffee steep for a minute and a half. Give it one more gentle stir halfway through if you like.

howToSteps.name: Press slowly
howToSteps.text: Press down slowly and steadily for 20 to 30 seconds. Stop when you hear a hiss. Add hot water to the cup if you want a bigger drink.

title: AeroPress Coffee to Water Ratio
tutorial: The AeroPress brews stronger than a pour-over, so the ratio is tighter: 1:13. The maker's own recipe is 17 g of coffee to 220 g of water, which is one heaping scoop and water up to the 4 mark on the chamber. It makes one cup in about two minutes.

The AeroPress accepts a wider range than any other brewer, roughly 1:10 to 1:17, because it is part immersion and part pressure brewing. The 1:13 standard suits most beans. James Hoffmann's lighter recipe runs at about 1:18, 11 g to 200 g, for a cleaner, filter-style cup. Start at 1:13 and move from there.

Water temperature is lower than for pour-over. The official recipe uses 85 C, about 185 F, which keeps bitterness down in a fast brew. Lighter roasts can take hotter water, up to 96 C. If the cup tastes bitter, drop the temperature before you change the ratio.

The chamber only holds about 260 ml, so a big mug needs bypass brewing: brew a concentrate at 1:13, then add hot water to the cup until it is full. A 20 g dose with 200 g of water, plus 100 g of hot water in the mug, makes a full-size cup without overfilling the chamber.

Grind medium-fine, like table salt, and press slowly. The press should take 20 to 30 seconds. Pushing hard squeezes fine sediment through the filter and makes the cup muddy. When you hear a hiss, stop: the coffee is through and only air is left.
